newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks end firmer, seen stabilising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks end firmer, seen stabilising.

text.p: Croatian stocks ended the week on a firmer note on Friday, with new gains for hotel issues and slight losses in blue chips, and were expected to stabilise following recent steep gains.
Traders said weak interest in leading issues -- drugs firm Pliva and particularly Zagrebacka Banka -- would probably cause their prices to ease before they can draw back serious buyers.
"But the market is expanding," Igor Kos of Taurus brokerage told Reuters and added:
"Hotelier (prices) are in line with this general trend. An excellent prognosis for this year's tourist season must also have something to do with it."
Nine of 13 active issues rose, three dipped and one was unchanged. Volume rose to 27,940 shares and turnover doubled to 11 million kuna.
Friday's most actively traded stock was food concern Podravka, rebounding 29 kuna to 539 with 17,642 shares sold.
It was followed by chocolate maker Kras, selling 2,269 units. Kras added 35 kuna or 7.6 percent to 495.
"It has been confirmed that Podravka will be floated and listed this autumn. But with Kras this is not entirely certain yet, hence the relatively modest trade," said Kos.
Top gainer was state-owned Adriatic pipeline operator Janaf, surging to 7,500 kuna, or 1,950 from a week ago as the market geared itself for its privatisation later on this year.
But volume was negligible and one trader described the price as "blown up out of all proportion" for the 1,000 German mark (roughly 3,560 kuna) face value of Janaf's shares.
Five of six hoteliers were also among the day's gainers. The only loser Suncani Hvar closed two kuna lower at 60 after trading 1,774 shares in a 60-63 kuna range.
Most active was Istraturist, rising ten kuna to 230, on volume of 1,444 units.
Arenaturist and Jadranturist each added 15 kuna to 175 and 350 respectively, while Laguna inched up three kuna to 1,498.
Fully-listed Pliva slid two kuna to close at 500 with 1,380 units sold. Its global depositary receipts (GDRs), issued at five to each share, traded at $16.5-17 in London.
The other blue chip, Zagrebacka Banka, lost ten kuna to 1,890 on a small volume of 54 shares. Its 1/10 GDRs to dipped to $31.875 on Seaq International on Friday.
